newsitem.title: USA: Mass. proposal targets dirty Midwest coal plants.
newsitem.headline: Mass. proposal targets dirty Midwest coal plants.

text.p: Targetting pollution from Midwestern coal power plants, Mass. Attorney General Scott Harshbarger has urged the 12 Northeast states and the District of Columbia to form a "Northeast Clean Air Compact", officials said Tuesday.

In a letter sent to the 12 governors of the Northeast region and Washington D.C., Harshbarger proposed that the states ban or place a surcharge on power from Midwestern states which allow dirty plants to operate.

The letter is the latest in a long battle between the coal-producing Midwestern states and the downwind eastern states where more than half of the pollution is caused by outside sources. Harshbarger fears the situation could worsen with deregulation of the power industry.

"As those plants unfairly flourish under market restructuring, they will send us even more of their dirty air," Harshbarger said in a statement. "Today's proposal fires a strong message to the Midwestern power plants and the states themselves that they should not expect to be able to compete in the big Northeast power market unless they clean up their act."
Harshbarger said in the letter the proposal, which would require congressional approval, may not be put in place, but nevertheless, could shift the debate in favor of the Northeast states.
James Milkey, the chief of the environmental policies for the Mass. attorney general's office, said the state is also frustrated by federal measures to try to stem air pollution.
"The goal obviously is to clean our air," Milkey told Reuters "We can't really do that without holding the big midwetern power plants to modern environmental standards."
Milkey said the letters were faxed or mailed on Monday and thus far, none of the governors has responded.
